conbody.p: With questions of who makes up the three-person tribunal in mind, establishing some kind of consumer advocate board, whose role would be to ensure that the process does not in any way take advantage of the defendant would be appropriate. This board could operate within the U.S. Copyright Office, working closely with the CCB to monitor for occurrences of policy abuse among claimants. According to media law professor Daxton Stewart, copyright trolling cases are highly unfavored among the courts. This means establishing a board to monitor for this behavior would be favorable to those who hear copyright cases. Moreover, because legal representation has been deemed unnecessary for the defendant when using the CCB, the board could provide legal counsel and representation for those who stand to pay statutory damages for copyright violations. The board could also have a hand in providing a mediation process in lieu of facing the CCB.
